authority_encoding.rule: Every component.authorities key is an authority dimension. Omitted dimensions mean no current decision authority for that component.

observed_product_path: ProductBridge non-terminal compatibility services when eligible

evidence: ProductBridge._chat orders IUE, CDM, cognitive capability analysis, memory, BCC, compatibility parsing, Kernel fallback and session writes.
ProductBridge._run_controlled_mission constructs the tool candidate, ToolAuthorizationGate, RuntimeNode and MissionRuntime invocation.
ProductBridge passes typed CanonicalTurnResult evidence to CognitiveResponseAssembler and serializes the governed CognitiveResponse without supplying final semantic fields.
Compatibility participation is attached only where a compatibility component actually executes; domain metadata does not infer participation.
Kernel.process parses with IntentEngine, consumes an RRM-owned provider selection, invokes _execute_canonical_route and PipelineDAG, then ingests PKB events.
Kernel._execute_canonical_route consumes capability_analysis but calls MissionEngine.complete directly.
Kernel.process always calls IntentEngine.parse before its provider/pipeline path.
ProductBridge._chat analyzes independent input before pending-dialogue matching.
IUE returns structured intent, domain hint, context and recommended capabilities but does not execute.
match_pending_response returns typed VALID_CONTINUATION, NOT_A_CONTINUATION or AMBIGUOUS evidence.
ProductBridge, not CDM, currently persists and resumes the resulting dialogue state.
ProductBridge delegates durable reads and writes to CanonicalMemoryService by project scope and authority key.
AME repository persists KnowledgeObject state, supersession, sensitivity and temporal validity.
KnowledgeObject models provenance, project scope, sensitivity, validity, supersession and retention; it performs no orchestration.
Session JSON stores derived pending_dialogue and known_context; Movement 11.5 proves these are not written to durable AME knowledge.
Kernel.process ingests PipelineDAG events through KnowledgeManager while ProductBridge separately persists user facts in AME.
KnowledgePipeline applies Constitution, curator, scoring/conflict decisions, store and audit to KnowledgeEvents.
CognitiveCapabilityRuntime calls discover for every ProductBridge chat turn before terminal/Mission routing.
Resolver evaluates capability.resolve governance and queries RRM for eligible resources.
Optional ToolRegistry participation exists in the class but is not wired by KernelBuilder.
Its CognitiveExecutionDecision is checked for terminal states and Mission before ProductBridge compatibility logic.
ProductBridge calls ECC during controlled Mission planning but uses the result only as an execution_graph identifier; CPE retains domain/keyword plan branches.
COR defaults to RegistryCatalog(populate_defaults=True), ranks agents/providers/environments, and is not fed the composed RRM in ProductBridge.
ProductBridge.dispatch exposes ECC results diagnostically; _run_controlled_mission does not use its assignments to select the synthetic action or tool.
ProductBridge regexes BCC FIRST_RUN_PATTERNS and directly uses BCC summary text before final response assembly.
KernelBuilder projects Core Apps, agents and providers into one RRM and passes it to CapabilityFirstResolver and MissionRuntime ActionGate.
Movement 11.4 adds CanonicalResourceBindingAuthority: execution bindings require RRM eligibility at selection and are revalidated immediately before dispatch.

Canonical ProductBridge/Kernel execution supplies an immutable CanonicalProviderAuthority selection; ProviderManager revalidates it against RRM immediately before returning an invocation binding. Direct Kernel callers retain an explicit compatibility default.
CapabilityExecutionService consumes CanonicalResourceBindingAuthority; registry membership and executor health cannot override RRM eligibility.
Explicit capabilities map to Core App bindings, but _DOMAIN_DEFAULTS still selects a capability when callers omit it.
The class creates its own InMemoryToolRegistry, permission manager and health adapter; KernelBuilder does not construct it.
Orchestrator owns an agent registry and first-compatible selection independently of RRM, then invokes with bounded limits.
ModuleRouter prioritizes Domain, then trigger words, then Core fallback and records a standard non-sensitive compatibility trace.
Adapter contains a compatibility Domain-to-capability translation, emits the standard compatibility trace, and cannot complete MissionEngine without canonical verification evidence.
Service selects from CanonicalCapabilityRegistry, evaluates capability.execute, dispatches app/agent/provider and proposes PKB knowledge.
MissionEngine owns create/start/pause/resume/complete and the MissionStore, but complete accepts no verification evidence.
Runtime owns a separate runtime state machine, ActionGate, executor, VerificationGate, MissionCompletionGate and checkpoints.
Tool registry stores independent tool statuses/capability mappings; the composed CapabilityFirstResolver receives tool_registry=None.
ProductBridge handles every non-ALLOW state before constructing or running MissionRuntime.
MissionRuntime calls ActionGate before executor; gate may deny, require confirmation or wait for resource and receives RRM.
VerificationGate emits CompletionEvidence for each executed node and controls SUCCEEDED versus FAILED node state.
MissionRuntime can set its own status COMPLETED only after all nodes and optional output contract are verified.
ProductBridge.dispatch sends typed CanonicalTurnResult evidence through assembler-owned semantic derivation and response.output evaluation.
Composition shares one engine across product.input, memory, capability.resolve, mission.plan, tool.authorize, action.execute and response.output paths.
Kernel executes the legacy DAG after provider and canonical-route preparation; deliver node produces final output text.

confirmed_authority_conflicts.finding: Services retain content and evidence ownership; the assembler now normalizes status, epistemic/confidence defaults and provider provenance before governance.
Verified runtime completion, direct MissionEngine completion and session-only completed labels are distinct current truths.
Canonical capability execution is RRM-gated and revalidated; provider lifecycle selection, ToolRegistry projection and COR catalog convergence remain bounded follow-up work.
MemoryAuthorityContract assigns current durable truth to AME/KOM, PKB to curation/projection, and session known_context to transient dialogue only.
CanonicalProviderAuthority selects and revalidates eligible RRM providers; ProviderManager is an invocation binding on the product path.
Explicit canonical capability selection is active. Callable Core App Domain defaults and legacy Domain/trigger mapping are now characterized compatibility paths with the standard non-sensitive trace.
